title: Joining with $lookup
idea: `$lookup` joins another collection into each document: it finds the matching documents there and adds them to a new array field.
points: `from` names the other collection; `localField` and `foreignField` say which values must match.
`as` names the new field. It is always an array, even for one match.
With no match, `as` is an empty array and the order stays.
`$unwind` on `as` gives one object per match; no match drops the order.

edges.label: matches
edges.caption: One customer matches: `{ name: 'Ana', tier: 'gold' }`. With no match, the list would be empty.

edges.label: as: who
edges.caption: The order leaves with a new array field `who` holding every match. Its other fields are untouched.

code.title: Orders joined to customers
code.caption: One join stage, used twice. Step through it, then press Run.

walk.text: Keep the stage in a variable so two pipelines reuse it. `from` is a collection name.
Match each order's `customer` to a customer's `name`.
The matches arrive as an array in `who`.
Match first, so only the two biggest orders are joined.
`'who.tier'` keeps only `tier` inside each element of the `who` array.
Join paid orders, then `$unwind` so `who` is one object.
Group by the joined field: paid revenue per customer tier.

pitfalls: `from` takes the collection name (`'customers'`), not the model name; a wrong name returns empty arrays.
Both fields must hold the same type: a string never matches an ObjectId.
Every input document is joined, so `$match` first to join fewer.

quiz.why: Ana has two orders, so two documents come out. Each gets `who` holding the one customer named Ana.

takeaway: Lookup returns an array; unwind it when you expect exactly one match.

starters: Should I embed customer data in each order instead of joining?
